adrs.title: Capability-complete, accessible CLI contract and tracing/config edges
adrs.decision_summary: clap stays as the parser for all four installed binaries. The Rev-3 plan already re-scoped an owned parser to XL after measuring roughly 33.8k lines across six clap-consuming sources with hundreds of derive sites, and this ADR does not overturn that estimate. What it adds is the reason a replacement cannot even be evaluated yet: the CLI contract is currently pinned by source hashes rather than behavior. There is no --help golden anywhere in the repository for any of the four binaries, the help/OsString/accessibility contract is a prose sentence enforced by a substring assertion, and no test asserts a nonzero semantic exit code from a real binary run. An owned parser could pass every existing test while silently changing usage text, wrapping, error wording, and exit behavior. Byte-level argv, help and error goldens are therefore the precondition, not a later refinement. Two clap feature choices are load-bearing and frozen here because a naive reimplementation would change them by default: wrap_help is OFF, so help wraps at clap's fixed width rather than the terminal's, and the env feature is OFF, so no argument is populated from the environment by the parser and every environment read is hand-rolled.

alternatives_considered.option: Replace clap with an owned parser now, per the plan's OWN (SAFE) disposition.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The plan's own re-scope calls it XL: roughly 33.8k lines across six sources with hundreds of attribute sites, and an owned parser must cover OsString and invalid UTF-8, the bare double-dash terminator, short clusters, negative values, global and flattened args, counts, custom parsers, defaults, value delimiters and enums, help text and exit codes. None of that has a behavioral baseline today, so parity is currently unmeasurable.

alternatives_considered.option: Treat the existing source-hash pins as the drift boundary and proceed.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The registry says so itself: a hash match is inventory evidence, not behavioral parity. Hashes detect that a file changed; they cannot tell whether usage text, option spelling, wrapping, error wording or an exit path changed meaning. They also cannot survive the replacement they are meant to gate, since an owned parser rewrites those files entirely.

alternatives_considered.option: Unify all four binaries on the shared ExitCode registry as part of the parser work.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Desirable but it is a user-visible behavior change, not a refactor. Only the asupersync binary consumes the registry today; atp returns std ExitCode SUCCESS or FAILURE, atpd returns a Result so a failure exits 1 through Rust's default Termination, and offline_tuner calls process::exit(1) directly. Scripts and CI already depend on those observed codes. Unification must be its own reviewed change with its own evidence, and this ADR freezes the current asymmetry so the change cannot happen silently.

alternatives_considered.option: Adopt the command vocabulary in src/cli/atp_command_tree.rs as part of the frozen CLI surface.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It is unreachable. No binary imports it: its only consumers are atp_config.rs, atp_workflows.rs and the module re-export. Its twenty-two commands, including config, ci, dataset, fuzz, release and archive, cannot be typed by any user today. Freezing them would invent a user-facing contract that does not exist, and would let a future refactor silently promote them.

alternatives_considered.option: Drop the tracing-integration edge from the cli feature to reduce the marginal graph.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The plan flags this as part of this ADR, and the bead requires defining tracing subscriber initialization so that removing env_logger or clap does not silence useful diagnostics. Dropping the edge without first specifying the replacement initialization would remove operator diagnostics. Deferred to the implementation campaign with that requirement attached.

preserved_public_symbols.note: The shared semantic exit-code registry: ten meaningful codes plus the valid range bounds, with out-of-range values collapsing to INTERNAL_ERROR. The registry contract already parses this file and asserts equality with the artifact, which makes it the strongest existing CLI contract.
The accessibility and machine-readability contract, and the part of it that is genuinely portable across any parser because it is hand-rolled rather than clap-derived.

COMMON_ARGS_HELP is the only frozen help text that exists anywhere in the repository. This file is hash-pinned by the registry yet is not listed as a source owner of any capability row, which is part of CLI-GAP-02.
Shell completions are a user-visible surface and the checked-in atp completion scripts are the de facto command-name golden for that binary.

The re-export facade. Frozen for the paths it publishes, not as an implementation owner; see CLI-GAP-01, which records that the registry wrongly names this file as a source owner of the parser surface.

The command-tree roots of the asupersync binary: five top-level groups over five nested ATP trees plus trace, conformance, lab and doctor. This binary is the only one that consumes the shared exit-code registry.
A single-level command tree. Two commands are hidden from help and are typed with a double-underscore prefix; the registry records them without that prefix, which CLI-GAP-04 corrects.
The daemon lifecycle surface. Its signal handling is implemented here against signal_hook, not in src/cli/signal.rs, which the registry incorrectly names as its co-owner.
Five commands with two global options. Uses env_logger with a RUST_LOG-aware default filter, which is the diagnostics path the bead requires be preserved if env_logger is removed.

preserved_feature_flags.name: clap
preserved_feature_flags.effect: The parser for all four installed binaries. Only the derive feature is enabled. Crucially, wrap_help is OFF so help wraps at clap's fixed default width rather than the terminal width, and env is OFF so no argument can be populated from the environment by the parser. Both are behavioral defaults an owned parser would likely change without noticing.

preserved_feature_flags.name: cli
preserved_feature_flags.effect: Gates the asupersync and offline_tuner binaries and the whole src/cli module. Note the tracing-integration edge, which the plan flags for review under this ADR, and the env_logger edge that offline_tuner depends on for RUST_LOG-driven verbosity.

preserved_feature_flags.name: atp-cli
preserved_feature_flags.effect: Gates the atp binary. It pulls clap directly rather than through the cli feature, and pulls tls plus rustls-native-certs directly rather than the tls-native-roots feature that the capability row names.

preserved_feature_flags.name: atpd-daemon
preserved_feature_flags.effect: Gates the atpd binary and adds the tracing subscriber the daemon uses for operator diagnostics.

preserved_surfaces.note: Five top-level groups. The atp group carries twenty-two commands over five nested trees; doctor carries twenty-three. This is the largest command surface in the repository.
Single level, nine commands, two of them hidden. serve is a documented alias for recv and must remain accepted.
Seven lifecycle commands plus a four-action identity subtree, with root options for config path, log level, foreground and pid file. Signal handling is bespoke to this binary.
Five commands with two global options, verbose and output-dir.
Owned and parser-independent, so it survives any parser replacement unchanged. Adoption is currently limited to one of the four binaries; see CLI-GAP-03.
Hand-rolled and therefore fully portable across a parser replacement. NO_COLOR takes precedence over CLICOLOR_FORCE, a non-TTY stdout disables color, and CI or a non-TTY stdout selects JSON.

preserved_surfaces.wire_encoder: bash, zsh and fish completion scripts
preserved_surfaces.note: Checked-in atp completion scripts for three shells act as the de facto command-name golden for that binary.

No test anywhere captures --help, -h or --version output for any of the four binaries. This is the single largest obstacle to evaluating a parser replacement, because usage text, option spelling, wrapping and error wording are exactly what would drift.
No test asserts a nonzero semantic exit code from a real binary invocation. Only success paths are exercised end to end.
Twenty-two clap-derived commands that no binary imports and no user can type. Recorded so it is not mistaken for user-facing vocabulary and so a refactor cannot promote it silently.

preserved_wire_contract.protocol: command-line argv, environment, stdout and stderr, and process exit status
preserved_wire_contract.encoding: clap 4 derive parsing with only the derive feature enabled
preserved_wire_contract.signal_paths_note: Machine-readable output uses the JSON, StreamJson and JsonPretty formats; StreamJson is newline-delimited with immediate flush for streaming consumers. Progress reporting uses stderr while data output uses stdout, and each checks its own stream for terminal state.
preserved_wire_contract.help_width_policy: clap wrap_help is disabled, so help text wraps at clap's fixed default width and does not consult COLUMNS or the terminal size. An owned parser that wrapped to terminal width would be a visible behavior change.
preserved_wire_contract.env_population_policy: clap's env feature is disabled and there are zero clap env attributes in the tree. Every environment read is hand-rolled, which makes the environment contract independent of the parser.

preserved_config_semantics.name: binary_manifest_stanzas
preserved_config_semantics.contract: The four installed binaries are asupersync requiring cli, atp requiring atp-cli, atpd requiring atpd-daemon, and offline_tuner requiring cli and simd-intrinsics. Binary names, paths and required-features are user-visible and may not change silently.

preserved_config_semantics.name: color_precedence
preserved_config_semantics.contract: NO_COLOR takes precedence over CLICOLOR_FORCE, and a non-terminal stdout disables color. The -c/--color flag accepts auto and automatic, always and on and yes and true, never and off and no and false.

preserved_config_semantics.name: format_auto_detection
preserved_config_semantics.contract: CI being set selects JSON, then a non-terminal stdout selects JSON, then ASUPERSYNC_OUTPUT_FORMAT is consulted, otherwise Human. This ordering is the machine-consumer contract.

preserved_config_semantics.name: common_flags
preserved_config_semantics.contract: The shared flags are format, color, verbose as a repeatable count, quiet, debug and config, with the documented short forms. COMMON_ARGS_HELP is the only frozen help text and its content is part of the contract.

preserved_config_semantics.name: exit_code_semantics
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Success is zero, user error one, runtime error two, internal error three, cancelled four, partial success five, and the testing codes are ten through thirteen. Values outside zero through one hundred twenty-five collapse to internal error. Codes may be added; existing values may not be reassigned.

preserved_config_semantics.name: current_exit_adoption_asymmetry
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Only asupersync uses the shared registry today. atp yields zero or one through std ExitCode, atpd yields one on error through the default Termination, and offline_tuner calls process::exit with one. This asymmetry is frozen as observed behavior so that unifying it becomes a deliberate reviewed change rather than silent drift.

preserved_config_semantics.name: environment_reads
preserved_config_semantics.surface: hand-rolled environment access across the CLI
preserved_config_semantics.contract: The CLI reads at least CI, ASUPERSYNC_OUTPUT_FORMAT, NO_COLOR, CLICOLOR_FORCE, SHELL, HOME, USERPROFILE, HOMEDRIVE, HOMEPATH, APPDATA, XDG_CONFIG_HOME, PROGRAMDATA, HOSTNAME, COMPUTERNAME, SSL_CERT_FILE, SSL_CERT_DIR, ATP_RQ_AUTH_KEY_HEX, ASUPERSYNC_ATP_WORKFLOW_ROOT and RUST_LOG. Path-bearing variables are sanitized before use.

preserved_config_semantics.name: stream_routing
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Data goes to stdout and progress to stderr, and each consults its own stream's terminal state. Redirecting one must not silence or corrupt the other.

preserved_config_semantics.name: hidden_command_visibility
preserved_config_semantics.contract: The two double-underscore-prefixed commands are hidden from help but remain typable. Their hidden status and their exact spelling are both part of the contract.

preserved_config_semantics.name: alias_preservation
preserved_config_semantics.contract: serve remains accepted as a documented alias for recv.

known_gaps.summary: Four of the eight source_owners entries across the CAP-CLI rows do not own the code they are credited with. src/cli/mod.rs contains zero clap references and is a pure re-export facade. src/cli/signal.rs contains zero clap references and is not used by atpd at all, which implements its own signal listener against signal_hook. Cargo.toml is the manifest rather than source. src/cli/atp_command_tree.rs is clap-dense but unreachable from any binary.
known_gaps.consequence: Every CAP-CLI row names at least one wrong file, so a baseline built from these rows would inventory a facade, an unused module, a manifest and an unreachable tree while missing src/cli/args.rs and src/cli/output.rs, which hold the only frozen help text and the entire color and format contract.

known_gaps.summary: The registry's hash-pinned snapshot list and its source_owners lists disagree. src/cli/args.rs is hash-pinned but is not a source owner of any capability row, while src/cli/mod.rs and src/cli/signal.rs are source owners but are not hash-pinned.
known_gaps.consequence: Neither list alone is a complete inventory, and a reader cannot tell which is authoritative.

known_gaps.summary: The shared exit-code registry is consumed by only one of the four binaries. atp returns std ExitCode SUCCESS or FAILURE, atpd returns a Result so failures exit one through the default Termination, and offline_tuner calls process::exit with one directly.
known_gaps.consequence: The semantic exit-code set is aspirational for three of four binaries. Any claim that the CLI has a unified exit contract is currently false, and scripts depending on the observed codes would break if unification happened silently.

known_gaps.summary: The registry records the two hidden atp commands without their double-underscore prefix, so the recorded names are not the names a user types.
known_gaps.consequence: An implementer working from the registry would build the wrong command spellings.

known_gaps.summary: The registry pins exactly ten environment variables, but the CLI demonstrably reads at least nine more, including CI, SHELL, XDG_CONFIG_HOME, APPDATA, USERPROFILE, HOMEDRIVE, HOMEPATH, ASUPERSYNC_ATP_WORKFLOW_ROOT and RUST_LOG. The count assertion passes only because the test checks names against the seven hash-pinned sources, which exclude output.rs, first_run.rs and completion.rs where several of those reads live.
known_gaps.consequence: The environment contract is materially incomplete, and the test that appears to guard it cannot detect the omissions.

known_gaps.summary: No help golden exists. No test captures --help, -h or --version output for any of the four binaries. The help, OsString and accessibility contract is a prose sentence in the artifact, enforced only by asserting that the sentence contains the substring shell/OsString.
known_gaps.consequence: This is the central blocker for a parser replacement. Usage text, option spelling, wrapping, ordering and error wording are precisely what an owned parser would change, and nothing would detect it.

known_gaps.summary: There is no explicit handling or test for non-UTF-8 argv. Invalid UTF-8 is handled only implicitly by clap's PathBuf value parsers and one default_value_os_t. There is no allow_invalid_utf8 setting, no explicit OsString value parser and no test.
known_gaps.consequence: The OsString half of the claimed contract has no behavioral evidence, on any platform.

known_gaps.summary: No test asserts a nonzero semantic exit code from a real binary invocation. Existing real-binary tests assert success only.
known_gaps.consequence: The failure half of the exit contract is unproven end to end, which is the half operators and CI actually depend on.

known_gaps.summary: The CAP-CLI-OFFLINE-TUNER row claims the benchmark-adapters feature, but the binary's required-features are only cli and simd-intrinsics. Separately the CAP-CLI-ATP row claims tls-native-roots, while atp-cli pulls tls and rustls-native-certs directly rather than that feature. The registry documentation also states fourteen binaries while the artifact and its test say fifteen.
known_gaps.consequence: Feature and platform matrices built from these rows would test the wrong cells.

known_gaps.summary: The accessibility constraints that exist in code belong to the doctor TUI visual-language contract, not to CLI help output. They govern rendered screens, including alert-role distinguishability and avoiding motion-only state signals.
known_gaps.consequence: They must not be cited as evidence for the CLI accessibility contract, which currently has no executable coverage beyond the color and format resolution functions.

security_invariants: Secrets and credentials are redacted in output, logs and diagnostics; the ATP RQ auth key may be supplied by environment but must never be echoed.
Untrusted paths are bounded and sanitized before use, and path-bearing environment variables pass through explicit sanitization.
Arguments are never passed through a shell, so no argument can be interpreted as shell syntax.
TLS root discovery honors SSL_CERT_FILE and SSL_CERT_DIR as OsStr values without lossy conversion.
Suggestion and error text stays bounded against secret material.
The daemon binds and holds credentials with least privilege and its liveness checks resist PID reuse.
cancellation_invariants: Interrupt and broken-pipe produce a clean exit rather than a panic or a partial write mistaken for success.
Partial outputs are identified as partial, which is what the partial-success code exists for.
Signals cause a bounded structured drain with an explicit second-signal policy, and no child work survives the parent.
Progress reporting on stderr stops cleanly when stdout is closed.

platform_cells.note: All four binaries; the ATP config path has a macOS-specific branch.
All four binaries. Windows-specific environment handling covers PROGRAMDATA, APPDATA, USERPROFILE, HOMEDRIVE, HOMEPATH and COMPUTERNAME.
The cli feature is native-only and is rejected on wasm32 by an explicit compile-time assertion.

the atp binary and its nine commands
the atpd binary and its seven lifecycle commands plus identity subtree
the offline_tuner binary and its five commands

external_ecosystem_integration.accepted_providers: Shells, CI systems and operator scripts consuming argv, exit status, stdout JSON and stderr progress.

pinned_crate_versions.clap: 4.4 with only the derive feature; resolves to 4.6.x
pinned_crate_versions.env_logger: enabled by cli and consumed by offline_tuner for RUST_LOG-driven verbosity
pinned_crate_versions.tracing-subscriber: enabled by atpd-daemon for operator diagnostics

external_ecosystem_integration.no_reexport_note: clap is not re-exported and does not appear in any library public signature; the coupling is confined to the four binaries and the derive-carrying cli modules. That means an owned parser is an internal change from the library's perspective and a total behavioral change from the user's.
external_ecosystem_integration.runtime_seam_is_clean: The exit-code registry, the color and format resolution, the progress reporter and the completion generator are all owned and parser-independent, so they survive a replacement unchanged.
external_ecosystem_integration.removal_precondition: Byte-level argv, help, usage, version and error goldens must exist for all four binaries first, plus non-UTF-8 argv coverage and real-binary nonzero exit-code assertions. Only then can an owned parser be measured against the current behavior. The replacement must additionally preserve the disabled wrap_help width policy and the absence of parser-populated environment variables, or declare those as reviewed changes.

user_journeys.description: A user runs each binary with --help and with a subcommand --help and gets stable, readable usage text. Currently unguarded by any golden.
A CI job runs a command with CI set and receives JSON on stdout without color, without needing to pass a flag.
A user with NO_COLOR set receives uncolored output even on a terminal, and CLICOLOR_FORCE does not override it.
An operator runs atp send and atp recv, including the serve alias, and can resume or cancel a transfer.
An operator starts, queries, reloads and stops the daemon, and a termination signal produces a bounded structured drain.
A wrong argument produces an actionable diagnostic and a meaningful exit code. The exit half of this journey is currently unproven for three of four binaries.
A user installs generated completions for bash, zsh or fish and gets the current command vocabulary.

api_surface_delta.rationale: This ADR makes no source change. The CLI surface lives in binaries and in the cli-gated module rather than at the crate root, and the capability registry pins the api surface map by semantic hash.

supersedes.resolution: Reconciled to KEEP_UNTIL_PARITY, which is what the capability registry already records. The XL scoping and the listed parser obligations stand and are adopted verbatim as the replacement precondition; only the disposition label changes, so that the row cannot be read as authorizing implementation before goldens exist.

supersedes.stale_text: CLI surface: owned-parser contract (XL scope per section 5) and help/error-golden strategy
supersedes.resolution: Resolved by this ADR. The strategy is that goldens come first and gate everything else: there is no help golden today, so parity is unmeasurable until one exists.

migration_policy.additive_only: New commands, options and output formats may be added. No command, alias, option, short form, default, value parser, environment interaction, diagnostic or exit path may be removed or silently changed.
migration_policy.coexistence: clap remains the parser. An owned parser, if built, must be validated against the goldens before replacing it, not alongside it in production.
migration_policy.sequencing: Goldens first, then non-UTF-8 argv coverage and real-binary exit assertions, then a measured owned parser. Unifying exit-code adoption across the four binaries is a separate reviewed change with its own evidence.
migration_policy.docs_obligation: Any change to the frozen surface updates this artifact, docs/dependency_api_adr_registry.md, and docs/adr/dep_plan_adr_005_cli_contract.md in the same commit.

rollback_policy.trigger: Any removed or renamed command, alias, option or short form; any changed default, value parser or constraint; any altered help, usage or version text; any changed exit code for an existing condition; any lost environment interaction; any color or format precedence change; any stream routing change; or any newly required argument.
rollback_policy.action: Revert to clap and to the frozen surface recorded here. Because the decision is KEEP, rollback means abandoning the replacement attempt rather than restoring a deleted capability.
rollback_policy.verification: Re-run the focused ADR contract, the registry CLI surface snapshot test, the CLI output goldens, and the real-binary journeys for all four binaries.

required_evidence_classes: golden: byte-exact --help, subcommand --help, and --version output for all four binaries, which CLI-GAP-06 records as entirely absent today
golden: error and usage text for wrong argument, missing required argument, unknown command and invalid value
unit: argv parsing for short clusters, the bare double-dash terminator, negative values, repeated counts, global and flattened args, value delimiters and enums, and defaults
unit: non-UTF-8 argv on every supported platform, which CLI-GAP-07 records as untested
unit: color precedence, format auto-detection and stream routing under TTY and non-TTY conditions
real-binary: nonzero semantic exit codes for representative failures on each binary, which CLI-GAP-08 records as unproven
real-binary: representative journeys per binary including transfer, resume, cancel, daemon lifecycle, signal handling and tuner report
failure injection: interrupt during operation, broken pipe, and a second signal during drain
installed consumer: a synthesized install of each binary exercising completions and first-run behavior
feature and platform matrix: linux, macos and windows across the cli, atp-cli, atpd-daemon and simd-intrinsics cells
evidence.note: Naming these owners does not assert they have run. The existing CLI output goldens cover formatting only, not help. The doctor visual-language accessibility constraints govern TUI screens and may not be cited for CLI help accessibility.

cutover.note: This ADR authorizes no dependency exit. clap remains the parser for all four binaries. The tracing-integration edge on the cli feature is not dropped here, because the bead requires subscriber initialization to be specified first so diagnostics are not silenced.

adrs.no_claim_boundary: This ADR is a frozen decision and public-surface inventory only. It does not prove that the planned evidence has run, that the recorded command vocabulary is exhaustive, that help or error text is stable, that non-UTF-8 argv is handled correctly, that exit codes behave as documented on any binary other than asupersync, that an owned parser could reach parity, or that clap may be removed. It also does not certify the capability registry's CAP-CLI source-owner rows, environment-variable list, hidden-command names or feature claims, which CLI-GAP-01, -02, -04, -05 and -09 record as incorrect or incomplete.

adrs.title: Preserve Brotli RFC 7932 capability; KEEP incumbent until a full owned parity campaign passes
adrs.decision_summary: The focused pure-Rust brotli dependency stays, alongside flate2. The owner directive was already resolved in favour of KEEP before this ADR, and nothing in the source read argues against it. What the read adds is the precise scope a future parity campaign would have to match, and two corrections. First, the real codec lives entirely in src/http/compress.rs, which holds every brotli and flate2 call, the encoding enum, the negotiation algorithm, and the bomb-bound enforcement; the registry names src/web/compress.rs instead, whose only brotli references are inside its test module. Second, src/net/atp/compress/ looks like a second Brotli implementation with adapters and an engine, but it is orphaned: no module declares it, nothing references it, and one of its functions would not even compile on a default build because it imports flate2 without a feature gate. Anyone estimating the replacement from a naive grep would double-count a directory that has never compiled.

alternatives_considered.option: Remove Brotli and support only gzip and deflate.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Brotli is a live public capability in three places: HTTP Accept-Encoding negotiation, the public BrotliCompressor and BrotliDecompressor types, and the ATP manifest compression algorithm. It is also the default first preference in both compression middlewares. Removal reduces interoperability with every browser that advertises br, and the capability registry's no-claim boundary states outright that DEFLATE parity does not cover Brotli.

alternatives_considered.option: Write an owned RFC 7932 encoder and decoder now.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Only as a separate security-sensitive codec epic. The scope is an encoder and decoder, quality and window settings, streaming flush and finalization, output limits, interoperability with multiple producers and consumers, both HTTP and ATP behavior, a malformed and bomb corpus, and performance and maintenance cost. Compression codecs are a classic source of memory-safety and resource-exhaustion bugs, which is why this cannot ride along with unrelated dependency work.

alternatives_considered.option: Treat Brotli as cleanup that rides along with the DEFLATE campaign.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: This is the specific failure mode the bead exists to prevent. The two codecs share a module and a feature flag but not a risk profile or an evidence corpus. Bundling them would let a DEFLATE parity result be read as authorising a Brotli removal.

alternatives_considered.option: Reuse the CompressionEngine and BrotliAdapter under src/net/atp/compress/ as the basis for an owned implementation.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: That code is orphaned and has never compiled. No module declares it, nothing outside the directory references its types, and its gzip path imports flate2 with no feature gate, which would be a hard error on a default build. It is not a partial implementation and must not be counted as one.

alternatives_considered.option: Make the compression feature default-on to simplify the matrix.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Out of scope and a graph-size change in the wrong direction. The feature is correctly opt-in, and the identity path plus negotiation work without it.

preserved_public_symbols.note: The ungated half: the encoding vocabulary, the negotiation algorithm, the codec traits and the factory all exist without the compression feature. The factory returns None for the three real codings when the feature is off, so a build without it still negotiates and still serves identity.
The real codecs and the only place brotli and flate2 are called. This file is absent from the capability registry's source_owners, which is CMP-GAP-01.

The policy-bearing middleware. It owns the BREACH sensitivity guard and the only path that returns 406 when nothing acceptable can be produced. Its production code contains no brotli or flate2 reference; it delegates to http::compress.

A second, parallel compression middleware whose type name collides with the one in web::compress. It has no BREACH guard and no 406 path; it falls back to an uncompressed body. Both are public and both are frozen, because a consumer may be using either.
The ATP manifest capability the plan cites as a reason to keep brotli. Its Brotli branch is feature-gated with an explicit None stub when compression is off.
gRPC frame compression, gzip only. Frozen because it shares the compression feature flag, so a feature change reaches it too.

preserved_feature_flags.name: compression
preserved_feature_flags.effect: Enables the gzip, deflate and Brotli codecs in http::compress, the Brotli branch of the ATP manifest, and the gRPC gzip frame codec. Opt-in; not in the default feature set.
preserved_feature_flags.no_tokio_guarantee: Both codecs are pure Rust with no tokio edge.

preserved_feature_flags.name: brotli
preserved_feature_flags.effect: The RFC 7932 encoder and decoder. Used through CompressorWriter and DecompressorWriter with a fixed internal buffer, default quality 5 and window 22.
preserved_feature_flags.no_tokio_guarantee: Pure Rust, no tokio edge. No brotli type appears in any public signature.

preserved_feature_flags.name: flate2
preserved_feature_flags.effect: gzip and deflate via the pure-Rust miniz_oxide backend. Unlike brotli, flate2::Compression DOES appear in public signatures on the level-setting constructors, so flate2 is a public type dependency and not only an implementation detail.

preserved_surfaces.note: Entirely owned and dependency-free, so it survives any codec replacement. Implements the RFC 9110 identity rules, accepts the x-gzip alias, and breaks quality ties by server preference order.

preserved_surfaces.transport: HTTP response bodies and ATP manifests
preserved_surfaces.note: The capability this ADR exists to protect. Streaming chunk-at-a-time with explicit finish, poisoning on error, and quality and window exposed as plain integers rather than crate types.

preserved_surfaces.transport: HTTP response bodies, gRPC frames, ATP storage
preserved_surfaces.note: Separate campaign from Brotli. Note the level constructors take flate2::Compression, so a flate2 replacement is a public API change while a brotli replacement is not.

Owned and codec-independent. The limiting writer refuses a write that would exceed the budget before extending the buffer, so a decompression bomb never allocates. Every codec wraps it, in both directions.

Skips compression for responses correlated with secrets, keyed on request cookie or authorization or CSRF headers, a set-cookie response header, or a private or no-store or no-cache cache-control. Present in only one of the two middlewares.

src/net/atp/compress/ contains an engine, an algorithm registry and a Brotli adapter, but no module declares the directory and nothing references its types, so it never compiles. Its gzip function imports flate2 without a feature gate, which confirms it is not built. Recorded so it is neither counted as an implementation nor as replacement scope.
There is no zstd dependency and no zstd encoding. The token is deliberately used in tests as the canonical unknown coding. Recorded so the four supported codings are not mistaken for an open set.

preserved_wire_contract.protocol: HTTP content coding, plus ATP manifest compression
preserved_wire_contract.encoding: identity, gzip including the x-gzip alias, deflate as zlib-wrapped RFC 1951, and Brotli RFC 7932
preserved_wire_contract.signal_paths_note: Successful compression removes content-length, sets content-encoding, and merges rather than replaces the Vary header. Responses with 204 or 304, or an already-set content-encoding, are skipped, as is output that is not smaller than the input.
preserved_wire_contract.http_status_semantics: When a header is present and nothing acceptable can be produced, the policy-bearing middleware returns 406 with an explicit body. The parallel middleware instead returns the body uncompressed. Both behaviors are frozen.
preserved_wire_contract.collector_interop: Browsers and intermediaries advertising br must continue to receive Brotli.
preserved_wire_contract.negotiation_rules: Quality values accept both lower and upper case q, out-of-range or non-finite values drop the entry, a missing q defaults to one, identity defaults to one unless explicitly scored or suppressed by a zero wildcard, and a non-zero wildcard does not lower the identity default. Ties break by server preference order.

preserved_config_semantics.name: supported_encoding_order
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Both default to Brotli, then gzip, then deflate, then identity. Because ties break by server preference, this ordering is the observable default behavior and may not be reordered silently.

preserved_config_semantics.name: minimum_body_size
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Defaults to 256 bytes; smaller bodies are not compressed.

preserved_config_semantics.name: output_size_limit
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Defaults to 16 MiB. None means unlimited and must remain expressible. The limit applies to both compression and decompression.

preserved_config_semantics.name: brotli_parameters
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Quality and window are plain integers with documented defaults of quality 5 and window 22. Exposing them as integers rather than crate types is what keeps brotli out of the public API.

preserved_config_semantics.name: codec_poisoning
preserved_config_semantics.contract: After any error a decompressor is poisoned: its buffer is cleared and every later call returns the same explicit error. A poisoned codec must never resume and appear to succeed.

preserved_config_semantics.name: error_type
preserved_config_semantics.contract: All failures are std::io::Error. Limit violations use InvalidData with a distinct message for compressed versus decompressed overflow. No brotli type appears in any public signature.

preserved_config_semantics.name: sensitivity_default
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Sensitive responses are not compressed by default; enabling it is an explicit opt-in.

preserved_config_semantics.name: feature_off_behavior
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Without the compression feature the factory returns None for the three real codings while negotiation and identity keep working. Building without the feature must never fail to serve.

known_gaps.summary: The capability registry names src/web/compress.rs and Cargo.toml as source owners. The real codec file, src/http/compress.rs, holds every brotli and flate2 call plus the encoding enum, the negotiation algorithm, the codec traits and the bomb bounds, and is absent. The named file's only brotli references are inside its test module, so its production code contains no dependency-level compression code at all.
known_gaps.consequence: A baseline or inventory built from that row would read a middleware that merely delegates, and would miss the entire implementation. src/web/middleware.rs, src/atp/manifest.rs and src/grpc/codec.rs are also unnamed.

known_gaps.summary: src/net/atp/compress/ contains a compression engine, an algorithm registry and a Brotli adapter, but the directory is declared by no module and referenced by nothing. Its gzip function imports flate2 with no feature gate, which would be a hard compile error on a default build if it were live.
known_gaps.consequence: It looks like a second Brotli implementation. Anyone scoping a replacement from a grep would double-count roughly four files of code that has never compiled.

known_gaps.summary: The registry's baseline command names a web_compression scenario, but no compression scenario is registered in the e2e runner and the fixture is still marked planned.
known_gaps.consequence: The named baseline command does not currently exercise compression at all, so citing it as evidence would be citing a command that does nothing for this capability.

known_gaps.summary: Two public types named CompressionMiddleware exist, one in web::compress and one in web::middleware, with different behavior. Only the former has the BREACH sensitivity guard and the 406 path; the latter silently returns an uncompressed body.
known_gaps.consequence: A consumer can pick the weaker one by accident, and a security property present in one is absent in the other. Both are frozen here because both are public, but the divergence is a real defect.

known_gaps.summary: flate2::Compression appears in public signatures on the gzip and deflate level constructors, whereas brotli exposes no crate type anywhere.
known_gaps.consequence: The two codecs have asymmetric replacement cost. Replacing flate2 is a breaking public API change; replacing brotli is not. Any combined estimate that treats them alike is wrong.

known_gaps.summary: There is no Brotli-specific fuzz target. Brotli is fuzzed only inside the shared HTTP decompression target.
known_gaps.consequence: For a security-sensitive codec whose replacement would be a new attack surface, dedicated malformed and bomb corpora are a precondition rather than a refinement.

known_gaps.summary: The capability registry records evidence as planned while the capability baseline artifact records the same capability as executable and complete.
known_gaps.consequence: Two governance artifacts disagree about whether a baseline exists. The same disagreement affects CAP-FUTURES-STREAMS, so it is a systemic artifact-consistency problem rather than a one-off.

security_invariants: Compression bombs are bounded by construction: the limiting writer refuses an oversized write before extending its buffer, in both directions.
The sensitive-body policy is preserved, so responses correlated with secrets are not compressed by default.
A codec poisoned by an earlier error never resumes and never presents partial output as complete.
Brotli remains supported, so no peer advertising br is silently downgraded.
No unsafe algorithmic shortcut is introduced in any codec path.
cancellation_invariants: A cancelled body releases codec state rather than leaking an encoder.
A truncated stream is never presented as a complete body; finish is explicit and separate from chunked writes.
Streaming backpressure is preserved because codecs operate chunk-at-a-time rather than buffering whole bodies.

platform_cells.note: Both codecs are pure Rust with no platform-specific paths and no C dependency.

entry_points: HTTP clients and browsers advertising br, gzip, deflate or identity
asupersync::http::compress codec types for direct use
the two public compression middlewares
ATP manifests carrying a Brotli compression algorithm

external_ecosystem_integration.removal_precondition: A separate security-sensitive codec epic must inventory the RFC 7932 encoder and decoder scope, quality and window settings, streaming flush and finalization, output limits, interoperability with multiple independent producers and consumers, both HTTP and ATP behavior, a malformed and bomb corpus, and performance and maintenance cost. user_journeys.description: A browser sends Accept-Encoding including br and receives a Brotli-encoded response with the correct Content-Encoding and a merged Vary header.
A client expresses quality preferences and the server honours them, falling back to server preference order only on a tie.
A client that accepts nothing compressible still receives a correct identity response, and a client that explicitly rejects identity receives 406 from the policy-bearing middleware.

A response correlated with a session cookie or an authorization header is not compressed by default, mitigating BREACH-style oracles.
An ATP manifest records Brotli as its compression algorithm and the compressed length is computed for the policy.

adrs.title: Preserve full futures-lite production semantics, public Stream usability, and test executor workflows
adrs.decision_summary: futures-lite stays. The classification the bead demands turns a scary number into a precise one: of roughly 796 references across 148 files under src, essentially all sit inside test modules. The production set is six sites in five files. But the shape of those six is what decides this. Exactly one is a public trait impl: AtpWriter and AtpReader implement futures_lite::Stream, which is downstream-visible and semver-relevant, and is the only impl of that foreign trait anywhere in the crate. Two are the FutureExt panic-containment boundary in the web layer. Three are the executor itself, block_on, one of them inside the body of the public non-async Router::handle and two driving signal-listener threads. The plan classifies this as a Phase-2 low-risk leaf removal over disjoint files with a util/future.rs shim; that is wrong on every count. The file set is roughly 272 including tests, not disjoint, and the proposed shim covers five helpers while missing poll_once, join_all, pending, FutureExt::catch_unwind and Stream entirely.

alternatives_considered.option: Move the helpers to an owned util/future.rs and drop futures-lite, per the plan's Phase-2 entry.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The shim list is incomplete and the framing is wrong. It names block_on, poll_fn, zip, race and yield_now, but production and tests also use poll_once, join_all and pending, and neither FutureExt::catch_unwind nor the Stream trait is a free function that a helper module can provide. The work also touches roughly 272 files rather than a disjoint few, which contradicts the phase's own parallelism premise.

alternatives_considered.option: Port AtpWriter and AtpReader to the crate's own Stream trait, removing the last public futures-lite surface.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Attractive and probably correct eventually, but it is a breaking change for any downstream already calling futures_lite::StreamExt methods on those types, and it currently has zero test coverage to protect it. It is recorded as the specific, bounded step that would remove all public leakage, and it belongs to the implementation campaign with downstream-consumer evidence attached.

alternatives_considered.option: Keep futures-lite only as a dev-dependency for tests.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Impossible as things stand. There is no dev-dependency entry today; the single unconditional entry in dependencies is what makes futures-lite visible to both src and tests. Demoting it would break the six production sites, including the public Stream impls and the executor inside Router::handle.

alternatives_considered.option: Replace the executor uses of block_on with the asupersync runtime.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The three production block_on sites are precisely where that is hardest. Router::handle is a public, documented, synchronous entry point whose whole async execution is block_on, and the two signal-listener sites run on dedicated std threads outside any runtime. Changing them alters reentrancy and nested-runtime behavior, which is exactly the contract the bead asks this ADR to define rather than to change.

alternatives_considered.option: Treat the roughly 149 non-test-file count as the migration scope.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It overstates production risk and understates total churn at the same time. Production coupling is six sites; total churn including tests is roughly 272 files. Conflating the two produces both a false sense of danger and a false sense of boundedness.

preserved_public_symbols.note: asupersync's own Stream trait, structurally identical to the ecosystem one plus a defaulted size hint, with blanket impls for pinned pointers, boxes and mutable references. Entirely free of futures-lite. This file is where the trait is defined and is absent from the registry's source owners.
The extension trait and the combinator surface, blanket-implemented for every local Stream. Roughly thirty owned combinators sit on top of it, none of which touch futures-lite.
Adapters over the local trait. Contains no futures-lite reference of any kind, which is why naming it as a futures-lite source owner is a defect rather than a rounding error.

The only place in the crate that implements the foreign futures_lite::Stream, and the whole of the public futures-lite surface. Publicly reachable with no feature gate, so the impls are semver-relevant. Notably this file does not import the crate's own Stream trait.
Panic containment is two-stage: a synchronous catch at construction, then FutureExt::catch_unwind at poll time. Only the second stage depends on futures-lite.
The error and negotiation handler's panic containment, gated by an explicit configuration flag. Uses the futures-lite stage only.

The highest-risk site. Router::handle is a public synchronous entry point whose entire async execution is futures-lite's block_on. The dependency does not appear in the signature, so this is a semantic rather than a type leak.
Two block_on calls driving signal-listener loops on dedicated std threads, outside any runtime. Replacing the executor here changes thread and reentrancy behavior.

preserved_feature_flags.name: futures-lite
preserved_feature_flags.effect: An unconditional, non-optional dependency with no feature gate and no dev-dependency entry. That single entry is what makes futures-lite visible to src, tests, benches and examples alike. It cannot be made optional or dev-only without breaking the six production sites.

preserved_feature_flags.name: default
preserved_feature_flags.effect: Recorded because the capability registry claims this capability is gated by default and test-internals. It is not gated at all: futures-lite is unconditional, so a consumer building with default features disabled still gets it and still gets the public Stream impls.

preserved_surfaces.note: A complete owned Stream implementation across roughly thirty combinators with no futures-lite dependency at the type level. This is the surface most downstream code uses, and it carries no replacement risk at all.

The entire public futures-lite surface, and the sole outlier from the crate's own trait. Any downstream can call ecosystem StreamExt methods on these types, so removing futures-lite silently deletes that capability.
FutureExt::catch_unwind is the poll-phase half of the web panic boundary. It is not a free function, so a helper-module shim cannot replace it; an owned equivalent would need its own future adapter.

Three sites, and the ones the bead's own description misses. One is inside a public synchronous API; two drive listener threads outside any runtime. These define the reentrancy and nested-runtime contract the ADR is asked to specify.

block_on accounts for the overwhelming majority of all futures-lite references and is the de facto test executor for the repository, reached directly or through per-module wrappers across roughly 272 files. There is no shared harness to swap in one place.
The util/future.rs module the plan names does not exist. Recorded so the plan entry is not read as describing something already partially built.

There is no adapter, blanket impl or conversion between the crate's Stream trait and the ecosystem one. The two coexist as disjoint, structurally identical traits. Recorded because the absence is what makes the ATP SDK outlier consequential.

preserved_wire_contract.protocol: in-process async execution; not a wire protocol
preserved_wire_contract.signal_paths_note: Router::handle is a synchronous public entry point that internally drives an async pipeline to completion, and the signal listeners drive receive loops on dedicated threads outside any runtime.
preserved_wire_contract.trait_compatibility: AtpWriter and AtpReader satisfy the ecosystem Stream trait, so downstream generic code bounded on it accepts them. That is a semver-relevant public property.

preserved_config_semantics.name: public_stream_impl
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Both implement the ecosystem Stream trait with a transfer-progress item type. Downstream generic code bounded on that trait must keep compiling, and ecosystem extension methods must keep working on these types.

preserved_config_semantics.name: owned_stream_independence
preserved_config_semantics.contract: The owned trait and its combinators must remain free of any futures-lite dependency, so the main Stream surface carries no replacement risk.

preserved_config_semantics.name: panic_containment_two_stage
preserved_config_semantics.contract: A panic during handler construction and a panic during polling are both contained, and both produce an error response rather than unwinding into the server. Only the poll-phase stage depends on futures-lite.

preserved_config_semantics.name: synchronous_public_entry
preserved_config_semantics.contract: A synchronous, non-async public entry point that drives its pipeline to completion. Its blocking behavior, and the fact that it does not require an ambient runtime, are part of the contract.

preserved_config_semantics.name: signal_listener_threads
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Listener loops run on dedicated std threads and block on receive. They must not require an ambient runtime and must not be starved by one.

preserved_config_semantics.name: test_executor_availability
preserved_config_semantics.contract: A blocking executor must remain available to every test target without extra configuration. Any replacement must offer a drop-in equivalent, because there is no central harness to change.

preserved_config_semantics.name: helper_surface_completeness
preserved_config_semantics.contract: The consumed surface is block_on, poll_fn, poll_once, zip, race, join_all, yield_now, pending, FutureExt::catch_unwind and the Stream trait. Any owned replacement must cover all of it, not the five helpers the plan names.

preserved_config_semantics.name: no_hidden_executor
preserved_config_semantics.contract: No API may start an executor implicitly. The three production block_on sites are explicit and documented, and that explicitness is the contract.
